source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Aurora is Illinois' largest disclosed data center campus at 114 megawatts, but that figure is only 48 percent of the state's disclosed capacity because most facilities publish no power numbers.

The campus spreads 114 megawatts across 450,000 square feet, about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet, a density typical of hyperscale colocation. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, that is roughly 2,850 racks. The published specifications omit cooling technology and redundancy topology, so the building's ability to host dense accelerator clusters is unproven.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and only six with published power figures. Aurora's 114 megawatts is 48 percent of the state's disclosed IT capacity, meaning most of the state's data center grid load is not publicly known. The operator also publishes no total campus power draw, PUE, renewable sourcing, grid connection characteristics, or interconnect uplinks, so the campus's actual constraint on AI scaling cannot be determined from available data.
